title: Evolution from classical to ML-based quantitative finance
claim: Author describes historical shift from Black-Scholes models to data-driven machine learning in finance
mechanism: Traditional econometric models replaced by supervised learning, ensemble methods
assumptions: Historical market data patterns generalize forward
failure_modes: Model overfitting on specific market regimes

title: Statistical foundations prerequisite to financial ML
claim: Probability, distributions, hypothesis testing, correlation structures form foundation for financial modeling
mechanism: Sound statistics enables correct model interpretation, avoiding spurious correlations
assumptions: Market data approximately follow known distributions under certain conditions

title: Neural networks learn nonlinear price-feature relationships
claim: Deep networks can capture complex nonlinear relationships between market features and price movements that linear models miss
mechanism: Universal approximation: stacked nonlinear layers represent arbitrary smooth functions
assumptions: Relationship is smooth and learnable from historical data
failure_modes: Severe overfitting on limited financial data
Model extrapolates poorly outside training regime

title: LSTMs preserve temporal dependencies in price sequences
claim: Long Short-Term Memory networks can learn dependencies across long time series via gating mechanisms
mechanism: Gate functions (input, forget, output) control information flow across time steps
assumptions: Current price depends on multi-step history
LSTM capacity sufficient for observed dependencies
failure_modes: Curse of dimensionality with high-dim inputs

title: RL agents can learn trading policies via reward optimization
claim: Reinforcement learning frames trading as sequential decision-making, learning policies that maximize cumulative reward signal
support: Conceptual framework; caution on practical applicability
mechanism: Agent observes state (market data), selects action (buy/sell/hold), receives reward, updates policy
assumptions: Market can be modeled as Markovian
failure_modes: Reward hacking: agent exploits reward signal without generating real alpha
Exploration during live trading incurs losses
validation: Paper trading before live deployment required

title: Price series exhibit stationarity, autocorrelation, seasonality
claim: Financial time series can be decomposed into trend, seasonality, and noise components; stationarity tests guide preprocessing
mechanism: ACF/PACF plots, ADF/KPSS tests identify structure; differencing and detrending restore stationarity

title: ARCH/GARCH model volatility clustering
claim: ARCH/GARCH models capture time-varying volatility; volatility shocks persist, creating volatility clustering
mechanism: Conditional heteroscedasticity: past residuals and variance affect current variance
failure_modes: Long-memory effects not captured by standard GARCH

title: Modern Portfolio Theory: efficient frontier, Sharpe ratio
claim: MPT frames portfolio construction as optimization: maximize Sharpe ratio subject to budget constraint; efficient frontier traces optimal risk-return trade-offs
mechanism: Quadratic optimization of portfolio return vs. covariance matrix; Capital Allocation Line (CAL) adds risk-free asset
failure_modes: Estimation error in covariance matrix amplified in portfolio weights
Extreme concentration on small sets of assets
Does not account for transaction costs
validation: Compare equal-weight vs. MPT weights on historical data

title: ML can estimate better covariance matrices than historical averages
claim: Machine learning methods (shrinkage, neural networks, factor models) can outperform sample covariance in portfolio optimization
mechanism: Shrinkage reduces estimation noise; factor models exploit latent structure; neural networks learn nonlinear relationships

title: Backtesting requires correct regime handling, transaction costs, survivorship bias
claim: Valid backtests must simulate realistic costs (commissions, slippage), avoid look-ahead bias, and account for data selection/survivorship
support: Industry best practice; many papers on backtesting pitfalls
mechanism: Transaction costs reduce returns; forward-testing guards against overfitting

title: HFT execution requires microsecond latency and specialized infrastructure
claim: High-frequency trading demands subsecond order latency, market data feeds, and infrastructure beyond reach of retail/research setups
mechanism: Market structure favors low-latency participants; arbitrage windows close in milliseconds
failure_modes: Retail strategies compete poorly against professional HFT

title: Alternative data sources carry freshness and quality risks
claim: Alternative data (satellite imagery, web scraping, credit card transactions) can provide alpha but faces data freshness, completeness, and regulatory risks
support: Industry trend; specific examples likely cited
mechanism: Alternative data provides signals before traditional data; high-frequency updates enable faster reactions
validation: Paper trading with real alternative data feed

title: Feature engineering transforms raw price data into predictive signals
claim: Domain-specific feature engineering—momentum, volatility, technical indicators—increases model predictiveness and reduces dimensionality
mechanism: Hand-crafted features encode domain knowledge; reduces model degrees of freedom

title: Model deployment requires monitoring, retraining, and version control
claim: Production ML systems need live performance monitoring, automated retraining triggers, and model versioning to detect drift and failures
mechanism: Models degrade as market regime shifts; monitoring triggers retraining; versioning enables rollback

title: Ensemble methods reduce model risk through diversification
claim: Random forests, gradient boosting, voting ensembles combine weak learners to reduce variance and improve generalization
mechanism: Uncorrelated predictions from diverse models average out errors
assumptions: Base learners are diverse and uncorrelated
failure_modes: Correlated base models add little value
validation: Compare ensemble vs. single model OOS

title: Feature scaling prevents model bias toward large-magnitude features
claim: Standardization (z-score) or Min-Max normalization ensures all features contribute equally; unscaled features bias learning toward high-magnitude inputs
mechanism: Scaled features have unit variance; gradient descent converges faster; distance metrics become meaningful
failure_modes: Ignoring scaling breaks tree-based models interpretability
Rescaling test data on training stats causes data leakage

title: Walk-forward validation simulates live model deployment
claim: Walk-forward backtesting (retrain on expanding window, test on future period) more realistically simulates live deployment than static train/test split
mechanism: Each test period is truly out-of-sample; no look-ahead; reflects actual deployment
assumptions: Live strategy operates under walk-forward logic
failure_modes: May mask overfitting if hyperparameter grid chosen on full data
validation: Implement walk-forward and compare to static split

title: Value-at-Risk and Expected Shortfall quantify tail risk
claim: VaR (percentile loss) and Expected Shortfall (ES, mean of tail losses) provide risk metrics for regulatory compliance and position sizing
mechanism: VaR threshold; ES captures extreme loss severity
failure_modes: VaR underestimates tail risk in crisis

title: Correlation matrices drive portfolio diversification and risk aggregation
claim: Asset correlations determine portfolio risk; correlation breakdowns in crises reduce diversification benefits
mechanism: Portfolio variance = weighted sum of individual variances + correlation-dependent covariances

title: Live trading introduces slippage, latency, and partial fills
claim: Backtests assume instant execution at OHLC prices; reality involves market impact, slippage, partial fills, and latency costs that degrade returns
mechanism: Market microstructure: orders move prices; execution takes time

title: Book emphasizes ML tools over risk-adjusted validation
claim: Text prioritizes feature engineering, model architectures, and tooling; dedicate less space to risk management, drawdown recovery, regime detection than justified by practical importance
mechanism: Content allocation reflects author focus
failure_modes: Practitioners may underinvest in risk controls
